Commentary of al-Qasimi (Mahasin al-Ta'wil) on surah 74, verses 1–7:

(p-5968) In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

Surah al-Muddaththir

Meccan. Its verses number fifty-six.

Ibn Kathir said: It is established in Sahih al-Bukhari from Jabir that he used to say: "The first thing revealed of the Qur'an was 'O you who are wrapped up' (ya ayyuha al-muddaththir)." The majority disagreed with him, holding that the first of the Qur'an to be revealed was the words of the Most High: "Read in the name of your Lord who created" (iqra' bi-ismi rabbika alladhi khalaq), as will be explained in its place, God willing.

Al-Bukhari narrated: "From Yahya ibn Kathir, who said: I asked Abu Salama ibn Abd al-Rahman about the first thing revealed of the Qur'an. He said: 'O you who are wrapped up.' I said: They say, 'Read in the name of your Lord who created' [al-Alaq: 1]. Abu Salama said: I asked Jabir ibn Abd Allah about that, and I said to him what you have said to me. Jabir said: I will not tell you except what the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) told us. He said: 'I stayed in seclusion at Hira'. When I completed my period of seclusion, I descended, and I was called. I looked to my right and saw nothing; I looked to my left and saw nothing; I looked in front of me and saw nothing; I looked behind me and saw nothing. Then I raised my head and saw something. I came to Khadija and said: "Wrap me up, and pour cold water over me." So they wrapped me up and poured cold water over me. Then there was revealed: "O you who are wrapped up. Arise and warn" [al-Muddaththir: 1–2].'"

The two Shaykhs (al-Bukhari and Muslim) also narrated from al-Zuhri, who said: Abu Salama ibn Abd al-Rahman informed me, "from Jabir ibn Abd Allah, who said: I heard the Prophet (ﷺ) speaking about the interruption of revelation (fatrat al-wahy). In his account he said: 'While I was walking, I heard a voice from the sky. I raised my head, and behold, the angel who had come to me at Hira' was sitting on a chair between the sky and the earth. I was seized with terror from him, so I returned and said: "Cover me, cover me!" So they covered me, and Allah the Most High revealed: "O you who are wrapped up..."' the verses."

Ibn Kathir said: This sequence is the preserved one, and it implies that revelation had come before this, given his saying, "the angel who had come to me at Hira'," which was Jibril when he came to him with the words "Read in the name of your Lord who created." Then after this there occurred an interruption, and then the angel descended again. This is the way of reconciling the reports: that the first thing revealed after this interruption of revelation was this surah.

Al-Tabarani narrated from Ibn Abbas that al-Walid ibn al-Mughira prepared food for the Quraysh. When they had eaten from it, he said: "What do you say about this man?" Some of them said: "He is a sorcerer." Others said: "He is not a sorcerer." Some said: "He is a soothsayer." Others said: "He is not a soothsayer." Some said: "He is a poet." Others said: "He is not a poet." Some said: "It is magic that is transmitted (siHr yu'thar)." Their opinion then agreed that it was magic that is transmitted.

When this reached the Prophet (ﷺ), he grieved, covered his head, and wrapped himself up, so Allah the Most High revealed: "O you who are wrapped up..." the verses.

(p-5970) In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

Discussion of the interpretation of the words of the Most High:

[1–7] "O you who are wrapped up. Arise and warn. And your Lord glorify. And your garments purify. And uncleanness shun. And do not confer favour to receive more. And for your Lord be patient."

"O you who are wrapped up" (ya ayyuha al-muddaththir): that is, the one who has wrapped himself in his garments for sleep or for warmth, from al-dithar (outer garment), which is everything of clothing that is above the shi'ar (undergarment). The shi'ar is the garment that is next to the body. The original form is al-mutadaththir, which was assimilated (idgham). He was addressed by this on account of the condition he was in at the time of the descent of revelation, or on account of his saying, "Wrap me up," as has preceded. It has also been said that its meaning is: "the one clothed with the mantle of prophethood and messengership," from their saying: Allah clothed him with the garment of piety and adorned him with the mantle of knowledge. It is also said: "So-and-so was clothed (talabbasa) with such-and-such a matter." So prophethood was made like a mantle and garment, metaphorically.

Al-Shihab said: Either it is meant that he is adorned with it and decorated by it, just as the garment above the shi'ar is an ornament and adornment for its wearer, and it is likewise called a hulla (finery). The comparison with the mantle is in its being apparent, or in its encompassing. The first is more complete.

"Arise" (qum): that is, from your resting-place and your wrapping, or the rising of resolve and earnestness. "And warn" (fa-andhir): that is, warn your people of punishment if they do not believe.

(p-5971) Al-Shihab said: He did not say "and give good tidings" because it was at the beginning of prophethood, and warning is the predominant aspect, since good tidings are for those who believe, and that had not yet occurred at that time. Or it is a sufficiency, since warning necessarily entails giving good tidings.

"And your Lord glorify" (wa rabbaka fa-kabbir): Ibn Jarir said: that is, magnify Him by worshipping Him, and turn to Him in your needs, to the exclusion of other than Him, of gods and rivals.

Al-Qashani said: that is, if you magnify something and esteem its worth, then single out your Lord with magnification and glorification; let nothing other than Him be great in your eyes, and let everything besides Him be small in your heart, through witnessing His majesty.

"And your garments purify" (wa thiyabaka fa-tahhir): that is, with water, from impurities. Ibn Zayd said: The polytheists did not purify themselves, so He commanded him to purify himself and purify his garments. It has also been said: it is a command to purify the heart from what is abhorrent of sins. Qatada said: The Arabs call a man who breaks a covenant and does not fulfil it "one with soiled garments." When he fulfils it and makes amends, they say: "one with purified garments."

It is related from Ibn Abbas: that is, do not wear them in disobedience or in treachery. Then he recited, for Ghaylan ibn Salama al-Thaqafi:

"And by the praise of Allah, I have not worn the garment of a wicked one, nor have I veiled myself in treachery."

In the first interpretation the words "garments" and "purify" remain in their literal sense; in the second they are used figuratively. There remains a third view, which is to take "garments" in its literal sense and "purify" in its figurative sense, namely "making clear" (tabsir), since the Arabs used to lengthen their garments and drag their hems out of pride and arrogance, so he was commanded to oppose them. A fourth view is the reverse of this, namely taking "garments" as a metonymy (kinaya) for the body or the self, as 'Antara said:

"I struck with the stout spear his garments" (i.e., himself). For this reason he said:

"The noble man is not made inviolable by the spear."

Ibn al-Athir, in "al-Mathal al-Sa'ir," preferred the first view. He said in the third section of his introduction: Know that the basic principle regarding meaning is that it should be taken according to the apparent sense of its wording, and whoever goes to interpretation requires evidence, as in the words of the Most High: "And your garments purify." The apparent meaning of the word "garments" is what is worn. Whoever interprets holds that the intended meaning is the heart, not the worn garment, and this requires evidence, because it is a departure from the apparent sense of the wording.

Then he said: A meaning taken according to its apparent sense does not give rise to disagreement in its explanation. A meaning departed from its apparent sense toward interpretation gives rise to disagreement, since the domain of interpretation is not confined, and scholars differ in this. For one of them may take a weak aspect of interpretation and clothe it in his expression with a strength that distinguishes it from other strong aspects, just as the sword is by its striker:

"Indeed the swords, with those whose hearts they are, are like their hearts, when the two hosts meet."

"You meet the blade, on the boldness of its edge, like the coward in the hand of every coward."

End.

Sufficient as evidence is what the Arabs have of citations and proverbs. Usage is not confined to the literal. Indeed, the more evident sense is preferable and more fitting, and it is the mark of the literal.

(p-5973) As for the words of the Most High: "And uncleanness shun" (wal-rujza fa-ahjur): that is, abandon it. Al-rijz with a kasra on the ra' is like al-rijs, and the sin and the zay interchange, since they are among the sibilant letters.

Al-rijs is a name for what is ugly and abhorrent. It was used as a metonymy specifically for worship of idols, based on His words: "So shun the uncleanness of idols" [al-Hajj: 30], or for everything disliked in actions and character. The sentence is among the comprehensive words concerning noble character, as if it were said: "Abandon harshness, foolishness, and every ugliness, and do not take on the characters of these polytheists who practise uncleanness."

It has also been said: the intended meaning of al-rijz is punishment, and abandoning it is a metonymy for abandoning what leads to it of polytheism and sins.

So al-rijz is a metaphor, and it has been put in place of its cause. Or it is by way of an implied genitive, meaning "the causes of punishment." Or it is a figurative comparison.

It has been read with a damma on the ra', which is a dialect form of the kasra version; both have the same meaning, which is punishment.

It is related from Mujahid that with the damma it means an idol, and with the kasra it means punishment.

He (ﷺ) was commanded with this, though he was free of it, either as a command addressed to others by way of allusion, or the intended meaning is continuance in abandoning it.

"And do not confer favour to receive more" (wa la tamnun tastakthir): that is, do not give a gift seeking to receive something greater than it, meaning: do not give something in order to be given more than it. It is said: "I conferred (mananta) such-and-such on so-and-so," meaning I gave him, as He said: "This is Our gift, so bestow or withhold" [Sad: 39], meaning give or withhold. The basic meaning is that whoever gives has conferred favour, so the gift was named "favour" by way of metaphor. Al-Qaffal allowed that istikthar may be an expression for seeking a return in whatever form, exceeding the gift. Seeking reward was thus called istikthar, treating the thing according to its most common state. This is like the case where a woman marries while she has a child, because of the need for someone to raise her child, so the child was called a rabib (stepchild). Then the usage widened, and he was called a rabib even when, at the time of his mother's marriage, he was grown.

(p-5974) The reason for the prohibition is that the gift should be free of expectation of return and of the soul's attention to it, out of self-restraint, perfection, and loftiness of aspiration.

It has also been said: the meaning of the verse is: do not give a gift while considering it great; for the noble qualities of character are to regard a gift as small, even if it is large. The sin here is for counting and reckoning.

It has already been discussed in Surah al-Rum in the words of the Most High: "And whatever you give in usury so that it may increase in the wealth of people, it does not increase with Allah" [al-Rum: 39]. There is also a discussion of this verse there, so return to it.

"And for your Lord be patient" (wa li-rabbika fa-isbir): that is, patient in the face of the harm of the polytheists.

The discussion of the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[8–10] ﴿So when the Naqur is sounded﴾ ﴿that Day will be a difficult Day﴾ [al-Muddaththir: 9] ﴿for the disbelievers, not easy﴾ [al-Muddaththir: 10]

﴿So when the Naqur is sounded﴾, i.e., when the Trumpet is blown. Al-Naqur (the trumpet, or horn) derives from al-naqr (striking, sounding), in the sense of producing a sound. Its root meaning is the striking that is the cause of the sound. From it comes minqar al-ta'ir (the bird's beak), because the bird strikes with it. That is, since the sound arises from striking, the word was used figuratively for it, and what is intended by it is the blowing, because it is a sound.

﴿That Day will be a difficult Day﴾ [al-Muddaththir: 9], i.e., severe.

﴿for the disbelievers, not easy﴾ [al-Muddaththir: 10], i.e., not light, because of the kinds of destruction that will befall them. In His saying ﴿not easy﴾ [al-Muddaththir: 10] there is an emphasis that prevents it from being difficult for them in one respect and not in another, and it indicates its ease for the believers. Thus it combines the warning to the disbelievers and the good tidings to the believers.

Note:

The exegetes agree that these verses were revealed concerning al-Walid ibn al-Mughira al-Makhzumi, one of the chiefs of Quraysh, may Allah curse him. Among the account of him is what Ibn Ishaq related: al-Walid ibn al-Mughira gathered with a group of Quraysh, and he was the eldest among them, and the season (of pilgrimage) had arrived. He said to them: "O assembly of Quraysh! This season has arrived, and the delegations of the Arabs will come to you in it, and they have heard of the matter of this companion of yours. So agree upon one opinion and do not differ, lest some of you deny others, and your statements refute one another." They said: "You, O Abu 'Abd Shams! So say, and establish for us an opinion that we may speak by." He said: "Rather, you speak, and I will listen." They said: "We will say: he is a soothsayer (kahin)." He said: "No, by Allah, he is not a soothsayer! We have seen soothsayers, and his is not their mumbling nor their rhymed prose." They said: "Then we will say: he is possessed (majnun)!" He said: "He is not possessed. We have seen possession and known it, and his is not its choking, nor its frenzy, nor its whispering." They said: "Then we will say: he is a poet (sha'ir)!" He said: "He is not a poet. We have known poetry in all its forms: its rajaz, its hazaj, its qarid, its maqbud and its mabsut, and his is not poetry." They said: "Then we will say: he is a magician (sahir)!" He said: "He is not a magician. We have seen magicians and their magic, and his is not their spitting nor their knotting." They said: "Then what shall we say, O Abu 'Abd Shams?" He said: "By Allah! His speech has sweetness, its root is firm, its branch is fruitful, and whatever you say of this, it will be known to be falsehood. The closest of what is said about him is that you say: he is a magician who has brought a speech that is magic, by which he separates a man from his father, and a man from his brother, and a man from his wife, and a man from his clan." So they dispersed from him by that. They began to sit on the roads of the people when they came for the season; no one passed by them without their warning him against him and mentioning to them his matter. ﴿I will cast him into Saqar.﴾ That is, Jahannam (Hell). It is a substitute (badal) for ﴿I will make him climb a steep ascent.﴾ [al-Muddaththir: 17]. It is a badal ishtimal (a substitute of inclusion), because Saqar includes hardships.

﴿And what will make you know what Saqar is?﴾ [al-Muddaththir: 27] ﴿It leaves nothing and spares nothing.﴾ [al-Muddaththir: 28] Al-Zamakhshari (al-Zamakhshari, the author of al-Kashshaf) said: That is, it does not leave anything cast into it without destroying it, and when it has destroyed it, it does not leave it destroyed until it is restored. Or: it spares nothing and does not leave anything from destruction; rather, everything thrown into it is certainly destroyed.

﴿Scorching the skin of mankind.﴾ [al-Muddaththir: 29] That is, burning the skins, from the phrase "the sun scorched him" (lawahathu al-shams), when it blackens his outer surface and extremities. Al-bashar is the plural of bashara, which is the outer surface of the skin, or it is a collective noun meaning people. It is also permissible that the meaning be: "visible to people," from laha (to appear, become visible), with al-bashar meaning people.

﴿Over it are nineteen.﴾ [al-Muddaththir: 30] That is, from the khazanah (keepers) who are charged with its affairs and with authority over its inhabitants. In this there is an indication that the zabaniyah (guardians) of the otherworldly punishment surpass the zabaniyah of the tyrants in this world by manifold multiples, as a warning of the terror of the punishment and the greatness of its place.

Commentary of al-Qasimi (Mahasin al-Ta'wil) on surah 74, verse 31:

The explanation of His saying, exalted is He:

[31] ﴿And We have not made the keepers of the Fire except angels, and We have not made their number except as a trial for those who disbelieve—so that those who were given the Scripture will be certain and those who believe will increase in faith, and those who were given the Scripture and the believers will not doubt, and so that those in whose hearts is disease and the disbelievers will say, "What does Allah intend by this as an example?" Thus does Allah leave astray whom He wills and guide whom He wills. And none knows the soldiers of your Lord except Him. And it is not but a reminder to humanity.﴾

﴿And We have not made the keepers of the Fire﴾, i.e., its guardians, ﴿except angels﴾, i.e., and they are the strongest of creation in might and the most intense in anger for the sake of Allah, so that they are distinct from the kind of those who are punished, and so they show them no mercy.

﴿And We have not made their number except as a trial for those who disbelieve﴾, i.e., from among the polytheists of Quraysh. That is: only a number of such a nature that the disbelievers would be tested by it, so they make it a matter of inquiry and mockery.

Al-Jubba'i said: The intended meaning of the trial is the intensification of the worship, so that they may reason and know that He, exalted is He, is able to strengthen these nineteen to do what a hundred thousand strong angels cannot do.

Al-Ka'bi said: The intended meaning of the trial is the testing, so that the believers entrust the wisdom of specifying this particular number to the knowledge of the Creator, glorified is He. He said: This is among the ambiguous (mutashabih) matters which they were commanded to believe in.

﴿So that those who were given the Scripture will be certain﴾, i.e., of the message of the Prophet, may Allah's blessings be upon him, because of his informing them of the threat against the deniers and corrupters, which is confirmed by what they have. The lam is linked to the second "We made" (ja'alna).

If it is said: How is it valid that We made them in reality to this number, with the reason being the certainty of the People of the Book, the increase of the believers, and the dismissal of the people of doubt and hypocrisy, while their creation as nineteen is not a cause of any of that? The cause of what was mentioned is only the report of their number as nineteen?

The answer: the term "making" (ja'l) is applied to two meanings:

One: making a thing characterized by an attribute in reality.

Second: reporting its being characterized by it, and this is called "making by speech." That is: We did not make their number, by reporting about it, except as a number that necessitates their trial, for the certainty of the People of the Book... etc., i.e., We said that and informed of it for the certainty of... etc. He expressed the reporting by "making" to match His saying, "And We have not made the keepers of the Fire..." etc. This is what the commentators of al-Qadi established.

﴿And so that the believers will increase in faith﴾, i.e., in assent, in addition to their assent to Allah and His Messenger. ﴿And so that those who were given the Scripture and the believers will not doubt, and so that those in whose hearts is disease and the disbelievers will say, "What does Allah intend by this as an example?"﴾, i.e., so that they will be frightened by these nineteen.

Al-Zamakhshari said: If you ask: How did He mention "those in whose hearts is disease," when they are the hypocrites, and the surah is Meccan, and there was no hypocrisy in Mecca, which only arose in Medina?

I say: its meaning is: "and so that the hypocrites, who will arise in the future in Medina after the Hijra, and the disbelievers in Mecca, will say: What does Allah intend by this as an example?" There is in that only a report of what will be, like the other reports of the unseen. And that does not contradict the surah being Meccan. It is also possible that "disease" means doubt and suspicion, because most of the people of Mecca were doubters, and some of them were certain of the falsehood. End quote.

Al-Razi said: If it is asked: Why did they call it an example (mathal)? The answer: since this was a strange number, the people thought that perhaps Allah did not intend by it what its apparent meaning indicated, but rather made it an example of something else and an alert to another purpose. Therefore they rightly called it an example.

﴿Thus does Allah leave astray whom He wills﴾, i.e., His leaving them astray is by turning their choice toward the side of error when they witness the clear verses of Allah that speak the truth.

﴿And guide whom He wills﴾, i.e., His guidance is by turning their choice, when they witness those verses, toward the side of right guidance. ﴿And none knows the soldiers of your Lord except Him.﴾ Al-Zamakhshari said: i.e., none knows what each soldier has of the specific number, whether some of them are in a complete tens-group and some in an incomplete number, and what wisdom there is in the specification of each soldier with its number, except Him. No one has a way to know that, just as the wisdom in the numbers of the heavens and the earths and the like is not known. Or: none knows the soldiers of your Lord, due to their great abundance, except Him; so the addition to the number of the keepers mentioned is not difficult for Him, but for Him in this specific number there is a wisdom you do not know. End quote.

(p-5982) It is also possible that the sentence is a confirmation that what preceded is an example, i.e., that the believers are certain that their number was struck as an example of an abundance that is not customary for the disbelievers to hear. It is among His customs, exalted is He, to coin examples in His revelation; otherwise none knows His soldiers, whom He empowers to punish whom He wills, except Him. This is another meaning which I have not yet found anyone to have pointed out, and His saying supports it:

﴿And it is not but a reminder to humanity﴾, i.e., an admonition by which they fear the punishment of the Fire and the terror of its people.

It was said that the pronoun refers to "Saqar," and it was said that it refers to the verses. The closer to me is the first, for it is free of the claim that what precedes is parenthetical if the pronoun is returned to something else, and because it supports what precedes in the sense we have mentioned.

The discussion of the interpretation of His saying, Exalted is He:

[32–37] ﴿Nay, by the moon, and by the night when it withdraws, and by the morning when it brightens. Indeed, it is one of the greatest (matters), a warning to mankind, to whoever among you wills to go forward or to lag behind.﴾

﴿Nay﴾ is a rebuke to whoever denied the number (of the guardians), or Saqar, or the signs. Or it is a denial that they would have a reminder, because they do not take heed. ﴿By the moon, and by the night when it withdraws﴾, meaning it turns away and goes off with the rising of dawn.

﴿And by the morning when it brightens﴾, meaning it shines. Among the benefits of swearing by these things is taking heed of their benefits and deriving evidence from their signs, as was mentioned earlier in Surat al-Saffat.

﴿Indeed, it is one of the greatest (matters)﴾, meaning the great affairs.

﴿A warning to mankind﴾, meaning a warning to them. It is in the accusative as a tamyiz (specification, the grammatical term for a noun that specifies what is vague) following "one of", because of what it contains of the sense of magnification, as if it were said: "The greatest of the greatest is its warning." Here "nadhiran" carries the meaning of "indhar" (warning), like "nakir" carrying the meaning of "inkar" (denial). Or it is in the accusative as a hal (circumstantial accusative, describing the state) of what the sentence indicates, meaning: it has become great, giving warning. In that case "nadhiran" is a verbal noun interpreted as a descriptive, or a descriptive in the sense of "mundhira" (warning).

﴿To whoever among you wills to go forward﴾, meaning to hasten toward faith and obedience, ﴿or to lag behind﴾, meaning to hold back. ﴿Liman﴾ ("to whoever") is a badal (substitute) for ﴿lil-bashar﴾ ("to mankind"), meaning: it is a warning to whoever wills forward and success, or backward and ruin. Or it is a khabar muqaddam (fronted predicate), and ﴿an yatqaddama﴾ ("to go forward") is a mubtada' mu'akhkhar (postponed subject), like your saying: "For whoever performs ablution, (it is) to pray," and like the verse: ﴿So whoever wills, let him believe, and whoever wills, let him disbelieve﴾ [al-Kahf: 29]. However, the second reading is remote. Abu Hayyan claimed that the wording does not admit it, but this claim was not accepted from him.

**The discussion on the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:**

[38–48] ﴿Every soul is held in pledge for what it has earned,﴾ ﴿except the companions of the right,﴾ ﴿in gardens, they will ask one another﴾ ﴿about the guilty,﴾ ﴿"What has brought you into Saqar?"﴾ ﴿They will say, "We were not of those who prayed,﴾ ﴿and we did not feed the poor,﴾ ﴿and we used to engage in vain talk with those who engaged in it,﴾ ﴿and we used to deny the Day of Judgment,﴾ ﴿until there came to us the certainty."﴾ ﴿So the intercession of intercessors will not benefit them.﴾

﴿Every soul is held in pledge for what it has earned﴾: i.e., it is held as a pledge and confined by it in the presence of God, exalted is He. ﴿Except the companions of the right﴾: i.e., they have freed their necks by what they made good from their earnings, just as the one who pledged an item redeems his pledge by paying the debt.

﴿In gardens﴾: i.e., they are in gardens whose description cannot be grasped. ﴿They will ask one another﴾ ﴿about the guilty﴾: i.e., they will ask about them. The use of the form tafā'ala (the reciprocal pattern) here indicates abundance and intensity, as in the expressions "da'awtuhu" (I called him) and "tada'aynāhu" (we called each other), where the reciprocal form is used for repeated or mutual action.

Al-Qashani said: i.e., some of them will ask others about the condition of the guilty, because of their knowledge of it, and about what necessitated their punishment and their remaining in Saqar. The respondents will answer that we asked them about their condition by our saying: ﴿"What has brought you into Saqar?"﴾, i.e., through the tongue of condition or of speech.

﴿They will say, "We were not of those who prayed,﴾ ﴿and we did not feed the poor,﴾ ﴿and we used to engage in vain talk with those who engaged in it,﴾ ﴿and we used to deny the Day of Judgment﴾: i.e., we were characterized by these vices: preferring bodily comforts, loving wealth, abandoning the bodily acts of worship, engaging in falsehood, mockery and idle talk, denying the recompense, and rejecting the return.

﴿Until there came to us the certainty﴾: i.e., death, so we saw with our own eyes what we used to deny.

﴿So the intercession of intercessors will not benefit them﴾: i.e., of a prophet or an angel, even if it were supposed as a hypothetical impossibility, because they are not receptive to it. There is no permission for intercession for them, so there is no intercession, and so it does not benefit.

Ibn Jarir said: i.e., the intercession of those whom God has permitted to intercede for the people of sins from among the people of monotheism will not benefit them, so their intercession will not benefit them. In this verse there is a clear indication that God, exalted is His remembrance, permits some of His creation to intercede for others.

A similar verse is: ﴿When a sign comes to them, they say, "We will not believe until we are given what was given to the messengers of God"﴾ [Al-An'am: 124]; and the verse: ﴿And we will not believe in your ascending until you send down to us a book we can read﴾ [Al-Isra: 93]; and the verse: ﴿And even if We had sent down to you a book on paper, and they had touched it with their hands﴾ [Al-An'am: 7], and so on.

[p-5986] ﴿No!﴾ [Al-Muddaththir: 53] That is: their desire will not be realized, and the truth does not follow their whims. Or: their wanting that is not out of desire for faith, for what suffices them has already come to them, so they have no need to demand something else. Rather, they are rebellious diseases. That is why He said: ﴿Rather, they do not fear the Hereafter﴾ [Al-Muddaththir: 53]; that is, they do not believe in resurrection and recompense, and do not fear punishment, because they prefer the immediate life. That is: this is what called them to turn away from God's reminder and to refuse belief in His revelation.

﴿No!﴾ [Al-Muddaththir: 54] is a rebuke for their turning away. ﴿No! Indeed, it is a reminder﴾ [Al-Muddaththir: 54] ﴿so whoever wills may remember it﴾ [Al-Muddaththir: 55]; that is, he who takes admonition and acts upon what is in it of God's commands and prohibitions.

﴿And they will not remember unless God wills﴾ [Al-Muddaththir: 56] That is: their remembering and their admonition, because there is no power or strength for them except through Him, glorified is He. In this there is a comfort to his heart, may the blessings of God be upon him, from what used to trouble him of their turning away, and what he was eager for of their faith. ﴿He is the One deserving of piety﴾ [Al-Muddaththir: 56]; that is, worthy that His punishment be feared, and that He be believed in and obeyed.

﴿And the One deserving of forgiveness﴾ [Al-Muddaththir: 56]; that is, worthy that He forgive whoever believes in Him and obeys Him.
